title: altafiber fiber construction maps, excavation plans, and schedules — Crossings at Windmere

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Ohio Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide the following existing records concerning altafiber’s fiber-to-the-home construction, including work performed by contractors on its behalf, within this geographic area:

Crossings at Windmere, Westerville, Ohio.

The most recent construction plans, route maps, permit drawings, or construction-zone maps showing planned or approved fiber installation in this area. Please include available drawings showing excavation, trenching, directional boring, bore pits, and associated work within public rights-of-way or utility easements.

The most recent construction schedules, phasing plans, anticipated start and completion dates, and schedule updates held by the city for this area, including records submitted by altafiber or its contractors. Please include any separately maintained schedules for excavation and subsequent pavement, sidewalk, or lawn restoration.

Issued right-of-way, excavation, or other construction permits for this work, including attachments and conditions identifying the work location, contractor, and authorized construction dates.

If these records are maintained by construction zone rather than by neighborhood or street, please provide the records for the zone or zones covering the specified area.

My priority is the maps and schedules in items 1 and 2. Please provide those records as they become available rather than holding them until the entire request is complete.

I am requesting existing records, not asking the city to create a new map or schedule. Please provide electronic copies, with drawings and maps at their available original resolution. Existing PDFs are acceptable. If relevant maps are maintained only in CAD or GIS format, please provide the available electronic files.

If any portion is withheld, please identify the legal basis and release the remaining reasonably separable portions. If clarification is necessary, please explain how the relevant records are organized so I can refine the request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Alex Jokerst

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Shift Scheduling Request
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of all shifts worked by all Boston Police Department employees from 1/1/2025 to 12/31/2025. Please include the following fields of information:

City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID)
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name or initial
Assigned description 
Charged description
Start time
End time
Worked hours
Billed hours


I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at adasuss@bu.edu.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

title: Georgia Open Records Act request: subcontractor, LSBE, bid and payment records for MK Industries, LLC and Lewis Contracting Services, LLC Dear Records Custodian:

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Georgia Open Records Act request: subcontractor, LSBE, bid and payment records for MK Industries, LLC and Lewis Contracting Services, LLC Dear Records Custodian:
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Georgia Open Records Act, O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 et seq., I request copies of the following records for the period January 1, 2023 to the date of this request, for each of these two companies: MK Industries, LLC (Doraville, GA) and Lewis Contracting Services, LLC (Lithonia, GA).
1. Any LSBE/DeKalb First participation plan, subcontractor list, letter of intent, utilization form or joint-venture agreement, submitted by any bidder or contractor on any County solicitation or contract, that names either company.
2. Any subcontractor substitution, addition or approval request naming either company, and the County's response.
3. Any prime-to-subcontractor payment or utilization report submitted to the County that lists either company.
4. Any bid, proposal or quote either company submitted to the County as a prime, including for 2025-055-RFP and 2025-098-ITB, and the bid tabulation or evaluation for each such solicitation.
5. Each company's LSBE certification application, certification decision and certificate, and its supplier/vendor registration record.
6. Purchase orders issued to either company, and the County's vendor payment history for each (vendor name, date, amount, check or payment number, department and contract number).
If the Finance Department rather than Purchasing & Contracting holds the payment history, please forward that item or tell me where to send it.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

title: Georgia Open Records Act request: ITB 2025-100070, Consent Decree Ongoing Sewer Condition Assessment and Rehabilitation (CD-OSCAR); Legistar 2025-1265

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Georgia Open Records Act request: ITB 2025-100070, Consent Decree Ongoing Sewer Condition Assessment and Rehabilitation (CD-OSCAR); Legistar 2025-1265
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Georgia Open Records Act, O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 et seq., I request copies of the following records relating to Invitation to Bid No. 2025-100070, Consent Decree – Ongoing Sewer Condition Assessment and Rehabilitation (CD-OSCAR), and the resulting award to Kemi Construction Company, Inc. and Southeast Pipe Survey, Inc. (Board of Commissioners agenda item 2025-1265, not to exceed $44,836,173.90, approved as a substitute on February 26, 2026).
1. The solicitation as issued, including all addenda, pre-bid conference sign-in sheets and the plan holders list.
2. Every bid received, the bid opening record and the bid tabulation.
3. All records of the County's responsiveness and responsibility determinations for each bidder, including reference checks, LSBE/DeKalb First compliance reviews, any bid rejections and any bid protests with the County's responses.
4. The award recommendation memoranda from Watershed Management and from Purchasing & Contracting, and every version of agenda item 2025-1265 from its introduction on August 27, 2025 through February 26, 2026, including the substitute the Board adopted on February 26, 2026.
5. Records showing what the substitute changed from the original item, including redlines, memoranda and the statement read into the record, if any.
6. All emails, letters, text messages and meeting notes from August 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 that discuss the deferrals and committee holds of item 2025-1265 (December 15, 2025 through February 17, 2026), the "additional information" the Public Works & Infrastructure Committee asked for on February 17, 2026, or the substitute, sent or received by Purchasing & Contracting, Watershed Management, the Office of the Chief Executive Officer or any Commissioner or Commission staff.
7. All correspondence in the same period between County officials or staff and Kemi Construction Company, Inc. (including any @kemiconstruction.com address and its president, Rufus Oladapo) or Southeast Pipe Survey, Inc. concerning ITB 2025-100070 or the resulting contract.
8. The executed contract(s), notice(s) of award, notice(s) to proceed, payment and performance bonds, and any change orders issued to date.
9. The LSBE participation plan and the subcontractor list submitted by each awardee, and any later subcontractor substitutions or approvals.
10. Invoices submitted and payments made under the resulting contract(s), from award to the date of this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar
